title: Zen Sudoku Flow
premise: A full-screen neon-styled Sudoku game where the player restores a destabilized pulse grid by filling a 9x9 board before running out of strikes.
interaction_model: Pointer/touch-based cell selection with an on-screen numeric keypad for entering digits and clearing guesses.
objective: Complete the Sudoku board so every cell matches its hidden solution while staying under the mistake limit.
progression: Each run generates a fresh puzzle with a configurable number of empty cells; moment-to-moment progression comes from filling the board, while session outcome branches into win or fail states with instant restart.
theme: Futuristic zen puzzle, combining meditation language with glowing cyber-arcade visuals.
mood: Calm, focused, luminous, lightly tense when mistakes accumulate.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy Sudoku, mobile puzzle games, casual brain teasers, and polished audiovisual feedback.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core mechanic is Sudoku because the code explicitly generates, solves, and validates a 9x9 Sudoku grid.
High confidence in mobile-first interaction because the game uses pointer input, touch-safe layout, and an on-screen keypad instead of keyboard controls.
Medium confidence on intended difficulty breadth because only one puzzle generation style is present and uniqueness checking is not enforced.
Medium confidence on branding because the document title says 'Zen Sudoku Flow' while the visible badge says 'ZEN GRID FLOW / Pulse Sudoku'.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly full-screen HTML5 Sudoku game with a futuristic zen-cyber presentation. The player should see a glowing 9x9 Sudoku grid centered on a dark blue sci-fi backdrop, plus a glassy HUD showing elapsed time and a strike counter. The puzzle must generate a valid solved Sudoku board, remove a configurable number of cells to form the playable puzzle, and store the hidden solution for each square. Players interact only by tapping or clicking: first select a cell on the board, then choose numbers 1 through 9 from an on-screen two-row keypad beneath the grid, with a delete button to clear non-fixed entries. Fixed clues must appear bright and stable, player-entered digits should glow in a contrasting accent color, and wrong entries should turn pink/red and count as mistakes. Every correct placement should trigger satisfying particles, subtle vibration support, and positive sound feedback; mistakes should cause screen shake, harsher feedback, and eventually a fail state after a configurable strike limit such as 3. Keep a running timer during play, check for completion when all 81 cells match the solution, and show a polished overlay on win or loss with themed text, reaction media, and a single restart button for immediate replay. The overall tone should feel calm yet game-like: meditative branding, neon grid lines, soft glass panels, ambient looping music, and arcade-style success and failure cues.
